subject: Run-scoped one-time delegation, protected exact-CWD handoff, and launch recovery
source_of_truth: Agentops adapter journal, handoff filesystem, and harness state machine at implementation commit git:694db475eb3299f638bc0d5b1105ed7cf138cf75
Owner run/delegation operations and their idempotency semantics
backends: Adapter SQLite journal on a temporary local filesystem
POSIX temporary run directories with fixture-controlled ownership and permission metadata
actors: FakeOwner implementing run registration, one-time delegation replay, and revocation
FakeHarness implementing session creation, title lookup, permission inspection, and adoption
Test controller injecting crashes and restarting the adapter over the same journal
operations: harness session create, title search, permission inspection, and prompt

consistency.target: Safe recovery across one-time owner token, local SQLite journal, filesystem handoff, and ambiguous harness launch
consistency.object: One message/run delegation generation, served backend marker, per-run profile/token files, session identity, and closing receipt

invariants: Delegation is disabled by default and an unqualified run never receives the inbox decision credential as fallback
The SQLite journal stores delegation id, expiry, generation, and handoff state but never the token
An owner token must match vrd_ plus exactly 52 base32 characters before any handoff files are created
A metadata-only idempotent mint replay is revoked and followed by a durable generation advance and new mint; token files are never reread
The protected .sprintctl/backend.json marker and .vuoro profile/token are in the exact harness working directory and match owner repository and adapter profile identity
Foreign, symlinked, writable, or mismatched existing backend markers refuse before mint and launch without overwriting content
A recovered verified session is adopted without relaunch and keeps its delegation; an unverified launch outcome is never relaunched
Explicit revocation precedes result-linked; failed revocation remains closing and retryable
faults: Crash after owner mint before delegation metadata persistence
Crash after handoff file and directory fsync but before installed state persistence
Wrong-content, writable, foreign-owner, symlinked, or writable-directory backend marker
Launch intent recovery with an existing verified session or no verified session
oracles: Persisted SQLite row contains no token and generation/idempotency key advance exactly once on recovery
Fake owner records the abandoned delegation revoked and the replacement delegation revoked on settlement
Fake harness observes the exact served marker and profile in the session working directory and is created at most once
Refusal fixtures produce no delegation mint, no session, and no overwritten marker content
Receipt history orders explicit revoke before result-linked; retryable close remains open on revoke failure
limits: Bounded fake-owner/fake-harness examples only; no live Sprintctl owner API or host launch was exercised
The test asserts the client marker/profile wire in the exact harness CWD but does not invoke the deployed Sprintctl client against a live service
Synthetic ownership and mode fixtures do not qualify production Unix groups, ACLs, another user identity, Windows, or physical comfort
fsync call ordering is exercised but power-loss durability across SQLite and filesystem is unknown
Delegation qualification remains false and no host production configuration was enabled
